sources.README.md:
# Laboratory microscopy series upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.

Checks: warm cached startup progress, out-of-order frames do not roll back display while audit retains admitted frames, unchanged queue record fields.

sources.src/Workspace.vue:
<template><section data-business="Laboratory sequence transfer"><output>{{ owner.fileId || 'closed' }}:{{ owner.attemptId || 0 }}</output></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef,onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
import {Session} from './session.js';
export default {props:['host'],setup(props){const owner=shallowRef({}),session=new Session(props.host,s=>{owner.value=s;});onBeforeUnmount(()=>session.dispose());return {owner,select:f=>session.select(f),retry:()=>session.retry(),hide:()=>session.hide(),dispose:()=>session.dispose(),snapshot:()=>session.snapshot()};}};
</script>

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

rules.body: Apply when one reusable progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup may emit cached state synchronously, decoding may complete later or out of order, and audit/history has a different lifetime from visible presentation.
Install the panel listener before starting a source that may emit cached progress synchronously. Preserve later streaming and the original startup and cleanup interfaces.

Decide packet admission for its originating visit/attempt before decoding, including while startup has not yet returned a cleanup capability. Retirement immediately revokes further admission; physical listener removal alone is not the logical lifetime boundary.

Assign arrival identity before decoding, and publish only completions newer than the last displayed frame for that originating subscription/attempt. Commit freshness state before callback-capable painting. Compare arrival identity, not numeric loaded values: later full frames may legitimately decrease or reset.

Separate admission, retained audit/history, and visible publication. Already-admitted decoding retains its audit/history after retirement or a newer visible frame, while painting must recheck the originating visit and freshness. Reopening the same source creates a distinct visit.

Establish cleanup ownership before synchronous startup can navigate. Retire old ownership before reentrant cleanup; recheck ownership before installing a returned handle. Never let an outer startup overwrite a newer visit resource. Preserve idempotent removal and cancellation.

Preserve accepted retry commands and their entry-bound queue records across cancellation callbacks, including navigation during cancellation. Do not add an early return that drops an accepted command merely because the callback navigates.

Keep the repair scoped to panel reception, admission, ordering and their necessary lifetime coordination. Preserve diagnostic/audit consumer policy and original queue-record shape; do not generalize panel visibility policy to independent consumers.

Check warm cached bootstrap and later streaming, reversed decoding with every admitted audit retained, decreasing/reset frames, late completion after departure and same-file reopening. Exercise synchronous hide/switch/dispose during startup and cleanup, multiple startup packets, subsequent-packet rejection, retry cancellation navigation and diagnostic operation after stop.

checkpoints: Warm startup delivers synchronous cached progress, and later streaming continues.
When decoding completes out of order, an older arrival cannot replace a newer displayed frame; admitted frames still enter history.
A later full frame with a lower or reset loaded value replaces the display.
During multi-packet synchronous startup, hide, switch, retry, or disposal prevents further admission by the retired panel attempt, including before startup returns.
Previously admitted decoding can finish after retirement and retain history without painting the panel.
Reopening the same file preserves the new visit's progress and cancellation ownership.
Synchronous navigation during detach or cancellation preserves existing command and queue-record behavior.
Telemetry retains its existing startup, live observation, and delayed decode behavior.
Mounted component commands and lifecycle teardown continue to delegate to the session.
forbidden_effects: Do not add byteCount or otherwise change queue-record fields without separate authorization.
Do not suppress history for an already-admitted frame merely because its decode finishes late or its originating panel attempt retires.
Do not use file or shared-source identity alone to authorize visible publication after reopening.
Do not use monotonically increasing loaded values as the freshness rule.
Do not let an older startup or cleanup continuation overwrite or cancel a newer visit's resources.
Do not apply panel admission or display rules to diagnostic telemetry.
Do not modify tests or configuration, access scorers, reference implementations, or hidden tests, or treat evaluation observations as requirements.
lifecycle_identity: Each selection creates a distinct visit, including selection of the same file object.
Retry creates a new physical attempt within the existing visit.
The progress source is shared across attempts and visits for a file; it is not a visit identity.
Admission and visible completion must belong to the originating visit and physical attempt.
Arrival freshness belongs to the originating panel attempt and is independent of decode completion order and frame loaded values.
Each workspace has an independent lifetime.

obligations.text: Restore warm initial panel progress by establishing panel reception before startup can synchronously emit cached packets.
Decide whether the originating panel attempt can admit a packet before decoding it. Retirement must immediately stop subsequent admission, including while startup has not returned.
Preserve transfer history for every admitted decoded frame, including completions that are stale for display or finish after navigation or cancellation.

Publish decoded progress only while its originating visit and attempt remain eligible, and only if it is newer by packet arrival than the last displayed frame. Establish freshness before invoking callback-capable display handling.
Coordinate startup and cleanup ownership across synchronous callbacks so that retirement during startup or detach cannot transfer an old handle into a newer visit or disturb its resources.
Preserve existing transfer, retry, cancellation, navigation, notices, cleanup, and queue-record behavior, including entry-bound retry work when cancellation synchronously navigates.
Preserve ordinary streaming, subsequent uses of a shared source, independent workspace lifetimes, and the diagnostic telemetry consumer's existing behavior.
Keep mounted component command delegation, framework state projection, and session disposal on lifecycle teardown intact.

ordering_barriers: Register panel reception before feed.start() can emit.
Check originating visit and attempt eligibility before feed.decode(), rather than relying only on eventual listener removal.
Assign packet arrival order before decoding can complete synchronously or asynchronously.
Retain admitted history on decode completion, then recheck visibility and freshness before painting.
Commit display freshness before showProgress can synchronously reenter session commands.
Retire old ownership before callback-capable cleanup; validate ownership again before assigning a handle returned by startup.
Preserve the source's removal-before-detach ordering and inert repeated removal.
preservation: Queue records remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Accepted retry work remains bound to the visit captured by that retry, even if cancellation callbacks navigate.
Cancellation remains per physical attempt and repeated cancellation remains inert.
Already-admitted history has a longer lifetime than panel visibility.
Full frames replace displayed state, including legitimate decreases and resets.
Telemetry continues starting before attaching its listener and continues delivering already-started decode results after listener removal.
Public component and session interfaces retain their existing behavior.
scope: Panel progress reception, packet admission, decode ordering, visible publication, and necessary session/attempt lifecycle coordination in src/session.js.
Preserve src/Workspace.vue command and lifecycle integration.
This extraction returns structured obligations without modifying files; any later Action is limited to business code in /workspace.

Detach/switch checkpoint: preserve the new visit when physical listener removal reenters selection.
Ordered-frame checkpoint: preserve ordinary complete-frame progress updates.
Reverse-completion checkpoint: older decode completion must not roll the current display backward.
Frame-value checkpoint: a full frame may decrease or reset loaded values; preserve arrival identity rather than imposing a monotone numeric value.
Retry/cancellation checkpoint: preserve synchronous navigation callbacks during cancellation.
Retry checkpoint: replace a physical attempt without opening another visit and preserve queue behavior.
Reopen checkpoint: selecting the same file again creates a new visit while reusing its shared source.
Startup/hide checkpoint: preserve visit-bound admission when a synchronous progress callback hides the visit before startup returns.
Startup/switch checkpoint: preserve visit-bound admission when a synchronous progress callback selects another visit before startup returns.
Telemetry cleanup checkpoint: preserve the diagnostic consumer after its stop capability is used.
Telemetry checkpoint: preserve the diagnostic consumer independently of panel policy.
Warm-start checkpoint: the panel receives initial cached progress and continues normal streaming.

rules.body: Applies when a shared source can be reused across visits, each attempt has an independent subscription, and visible feedback can synchronously reenter navigation. The same data object does not imply the same visit identity.

For a source that may synchronously emit cached events during startup, register the listener before start(), and decide whether each event is admitted for its originating visit and attempt before decoding or recording it. If visible handling of an earlier startup event synchronously retires that visit, later startup events from that listener are not admitted even before listener cleanup is available; events already admitted retain the separate audit and visibility rules.
Once a visit retires, stop admitting subsequent events even if the cleanup or removal capability has not yet returned. This restriction must not depend on deferred physical cleanup.
For an event admitted before retirement, retain its audit exactly once when decoding settles. That settlement must not authorize the retired visit to admit new events or produce visible progress.

After synchronous reentry, the new visit retains its own UI and cancellation resources. Subsequent settlement or cleanup of the old visit must not take ownership from the new one. Preserve existing retry, cancellation and entry-bound record semantics.

Test subsequent events from the same source after synchronous navigation and before the outer startup call returns. Cover hiding, switching and reopening the same source separately. Independently check rejection by the retired visit, delayed audit of previously admitted events, and valid visible progress for the current visit. Cleanup tests performed only after return do not cover this window.

Limit this repair to progress-admission timing and lifecycle boundaries. Do not expand records or public interfaces, or change shared-source reuse, independent workspaces, retry, cancellation, navigation, resource ownership or the audit policy for already-admitted events.

rules.body: Apply when one reusable progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup may emit cached state synchronously, decoding may complete later or out of order, and audit/history has a different lifetime from visible presentation.
Install the panel listener before starting a source that may emit cached progress synchronously. Preserve later streaming and the original startup and cleanup interfaces.

Decide packet admission for its originating visit/attempt before decoding, including while startup has not yet returned a cleanup capability. Retirement immediately revokes further admission; physical listener removal alone is not the logical lifetime boundary.

Assign arrival identity before decoding, and publish only completions newer than the last displayed frame for that originating subscription/attempt. Commit freshness state before callback-capable painting. Compare arrival identity, not numeric loaded values: later full frames may legitimately decrease or reset.

Separate admission, retained audit/history, and visible publication. Already-admitted decoding retains its audit/history after retirement or a newer visible frame, while painting must recheck the originating visit and freshness. Reopening the same source creates a distinct visit.

Establish cleanup ownership before synchronous startup can navigate. Retire old ownership before reentrant cleanup; recheck ownership before installing a returned handle. Never let an outer startup overwrite a newer visit resource. Preserve idempotent removal and cancellation.

Preserve accepted retry commands and their entry-bound queue records across cancellation callbacks, including navigation during cancellation. Do not add an early return that drops an accepted command merely because the callback navigates.

Keep the repair scoped to panel reception, admission, ordering and their necessary lifetime coordination. Preserve diagnostic/audit consumer policy and original queue-record shape; do not generalize panel visibility policy to independent consumers.

rules.body: When a subscription can begin decoding before its listener is removed, bind both its cleanup handle and permission to publish a decoded value to the panel visit that started it. Install a provisional cleanup handle before startup; if synchronous publication hides or switches the panel, do not let the outer startup replace the newer visit’s handle. Listener removal stops new reception but does not itself decide whether an already-started decode may publish: after a switch, hide, or synchronous reentry retires the originating visit, its settlement must not update the panel. Preserve bootstrap and later updates for the current visit, including a later visit using the same channel. Verify synchronous bootstrap reentry plus delayed decode across close, switch, and same-channel reopening: retired visits produce no publication and the active visit still receives its bootstrap and later update.

A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

candidate_sources.README.md:
# Laboratory microscopy series upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.

Public checks are deterministic external examples, not hidden gold. They are executed after each submitted Action. Keep original task/source obligations. Checks: warm cached startup progress, out-of-order frames do not roll back display while audit retains admitted frames, unchanged queue record fields.
Use the declared runtime: java OpenJDK 11.0.27. The external adapter is not mounted in the model workspace; do not access scorer/reference files. Build temporary artifacts in /tmp.

import {Session} from './session.js';
export default {props:['host'],setup(props){const owner=shallowRef({}),session=new Session(props.host,s=>{owner.value=s;});onBeforeUnmount(()=>session.dispose());return {owner,select:f=>session.select(f),retry:()=>session.retry(),hide:()=>session.hide(),dispose:()=>session.dispose(),snapshot:()=>session.snapshot()};}};
</script>
